resumeCommentsHint: Select a heading to expand one comment at a time. Use the heading actions to locate, resolve, reopen, or delete without expanding.
resumeCommentsEmpty: Keep interview reminders or editing suggestions here.
resumeCommentsPlaceholder: Write a short reminder or suggestion…
learningCenter_tags_summary: Use tags to distinguish versions for different jobs and situations.
learningCenter_tags_step1: In My Resumes, right-click a resume card and choose Edit tags, or use the more menu in the upper-right corner.
learningCenter_tags_step2: Type a tag in the input and press Enter to add it. Remove a tag using its delete button.
learningCenter_tags_step3: Select Save to show tags above the resume name. When there are more than three, select the remaining count to edit them.
learningCenter_tags_tip: Copies inherit existing tags. Job-tailored copies also receive a company and position tag, or just the position when no company is entered. Tags do not appear in application documents.
learningCenterSubtitle: Find a feature and follow the steps.
learningCenter_intro_start: Fill in content, adjust the layout, then export.
learningCenter_intro_edit: Add content, change its order, and control visibility.
learningCenter_intro_writing: Find writing tips and common questions by section.
learningCenter_intro_layout: Adjust fonts, spacing, and styles, then check pages and preview.
learningCenter_intro_ai: Work on the whole resume or a single description with AI.
learningCenter_intro_export: Check save status, back up data, and export files to send or share.
learningCenter_workspace_summary: Edit on the left and preview the layout on the right.
learningCenter_workspace_step1: Fill in personal information and add sections in the Edit tab.
learningCenter_workspace_step2: Choose a style in Templates and adjust it in the preview toolbar.
learningCenter_workspace_step3: Check the preview, then select Export Resume in the header.
learningCenter_workspace_tip: Interface language does not translate content. Use translation in the AI tab.
learningCenter_import_summary: Import PDF, Markdown, or a JSON backup from this tool.
learningCenter_import_step1: Open More Actions at the bottom left and select Import Resume.
learningCenter_import_step2: Choose PDF or Markdown to parse content, or JSON to restore a full backup.
learningCenter_import_step3: For PDF and Markdown, review the parsed preview before confirming.
learningCenter_import_tip: PDF and Markdown require a configured parsing model.
learningCenter_modules_summary: Resize section navigation, add, rename, reorder, or hide a whole section.
learningCenter_modules_step1: Choose a section in the add menu, or use Add All for common sections. Click the handle on the right edge of the section tree to collapse navigation, and click the handle on the left edge to restore it. On mobile, tap the left-edge handle to slide out the navigation drawer.
learningCenter_modules_step2: Select the heading pencil to rename it. Drag its handle to reorder it.
learningCenter_modules_step3: Use the eye to hide a section or the trash icon to delete it.
learningCenter_modules_tip: Personal Information stays fixed. Add Job Preferences from Add Module to move existing job fields there; deleting it moves them back to the end of Personal Information. Your work start date stays in place. Collapsing does not hide content; Show All restores it.
learningCenter_fields_summary: Add common fields, custom fields, a photo, or a school logo.
learningCenter_fields_step1: Add common fields below personal information. Find other fields in More.
learningCenter_fields_step2: Add a custom field, edit its label, and enter its value.
learningCenter_fields_step3: Upload an image in the photo or logo card, confirm the crop, and preview it.
learningCenter_fields_tip: Use the eye icon to hide a field. Select Export photo to download an uploaded photo.
learningCenter_records_summary: Add multiple jobs, education entries, or projects to a section.
learningCenter_records_step1: Use the add action at the bottom of a section to create an entry.
learningCenter_records_step2: Copy an entry with its copy icon. Drag its handle to reorder it.
learningCenter_records_step3: Use the entry's eye to hide it or its trash icon to delete it. On desktop, hover over a section or entry and use the icon outside the page to add comments; the count is the section total. On mobile, select Comments at the bottom right to view all comments or filter by section. Cards show two-line summaries by default. Select a heading to expand one card at a time. Heading actions remain available while collapsed to locate, resolve, reopen, or delete. Text edits preserve the link; comments move and are deleted with their entry. Comments save automatically and are excluded from application exports.
learningCenter_records_tip: Smart Sort orders entries by date. Use the first description toolbar icon to toggle plain-text paste.
learningCenter_checks_summary: Find missing fields, format issues, and date issues.
learningCenter_checks_step1: Select completeness or the pending-issue prompt above the section list.
learningCenter_checks_step2: Select Edit beside a specific issue to expand and locate the relevant section or entry.
learningCenter_checks_step3: For AI help, use the adjacent adjustment or optimization action.
learningCenter_checks_tip: Issues update as you edit. Completeness measures required information, not recruitment screening results.
learningCenter_style_summary: Choose a template, then adjust its options in the preview toolbar.
learningCenter_style_step1: Choose an appearance in Templates on the left.
learningCenter_style_step2: Use Design for colors and backgrounds, and Layout for placement and alignment.
learningCenter_style_step3: Use Details for date formats and information separators.
learningCenter_style_tip: Reset restores template defaults. Restricted options show a reason. The footer is off by default, and its visibility is saved and backed up with each resume. Switching templates preserves footer settings. When off, the custom bottom margin applies. When on, the bottom space is the larger of the bottom margin and footer height, which may change pagination.
learningCenter_spacing_summary: Set text size, grayscale, and spacing in the preview toolbar.
learningCenter_spacing_step1: At the far left, select the font name, size, or underlined A to adjust font grayscale.
learningCenter_spacing_step2: Open Spacing to adjust top, bottom, and horizontal margins independently, along with section and paragraph spacing and line height.
learningCenter_spacing_step3: Try Smart One-Page Fit when content slightly exceeds one page. Body text stays at least 14px and shrinks by no more than 2px per attempt.
learningCenter_spacing_tip: A successful fit creates one history entry. If readable content cannot fit, the original layout is restored; shorten the content or keep multiple pages.
learningCenter_preview_summary: Change viewing scale and check page count and grayscale appearance.
learningCenter_preview_step1: Open Zoom and choose one-page view, adaptive view, standard A4, or a percentage. Select Hide comments beside Zoom to collapse cards and lines while keeping add controls and counts visible. Select a count to show comments again. Hiding does not delete comments.
learningCenter_preview_step2: Check page count and breaks for complete text and images.
learningCenter_preview_step3: Use grayscale mode for black-and-white viewing, or open Fullscreen Preview.
learningCenter_preview_tip: Zoom changes the view, not font sizes or pagination.
learningCenter_assistant_summary: Draft, optimize, translate, or tailor your resume to a job.
learningCenter_assistant_step1: In AI Settings on the right, select a model for Resume Assistant Xiaozhou under Role Models.
learningCenter_assistant_step2: Choose a resume task or type a request in the AI tab on the left. Select target sections first for local changes. For interview practice, return to the workspace, open AI Interview, and assign a model independently to Interviewer Xiaoyang.
learningCenter_assistant_step3: Review View Changes afterward, or use conversation undo to restore content.
learningCenter_assistant_tip: In AI Settings, select a provider and enter its API key and endpoint URL. Configuration is saved automatically. Click Add Model to select a common model or enter its full API model ID and an optional display alias, then test the connection to add it. Presets only help fill the form; users maintain subsequent model changes themselves. Manage existing models under their provider and assign them in Role Models. The default scope is the whole resume; check scope instructions for whole-resume tasks.
learningCenter_jobMatch_summary: Compare your resume with job requirements and save a dedicated version.
learningCenter_jobMatch_step1: Open AI Job Matching in the workspace to enter the tailoring form directly.
learningCenter_jobMatch_step2: Select a resume, enter the target role and paste its requirements, then generate a tailored draft.
learningCenter_jobMatch_step3: Review the report, resume or comparison, then save a dedicated version. Score sections remain hidden when no valid scores are available.
learningCenter_jobMatch_tip: Uses the Resume Assistant Xiaozhou model and current privacy settings. Skills missing from the resume require confirmation. The resume limit is checked before starting job matching. If full, delete an unneeded resume in My Resumes before use. Capacity is checked again when saving; the original is preserved.
learningCenter_contentAi_summary: Generate, continue, or rewrite the current text field.
learningCenter_contentAi_step1: Open the field's AI menu and choose Generate or Continue.
learningCenter_contentAi_step2: To rewrite, choose More professional, More concise, or More detailed.
learningCenter_contentAi_step3: Review candidates in the result panel and select Apply.
learningCenter_contentAi_tip: Check facts and XX placeholders, and keep any manual edits you need.
learningCenter_save_summary: Edits save automatically. You can also export a full backup.
learningCenter_save_step1: Check save status beside the title after editing.
learningCenter_save_step2: Use header undo and redo to move through editing history.
learningCenter_save_step3: In supported browsers, authorize a backup folder, or export full JSON.
learningCenter_save_tip: Local data does not sync across devices. Export JSON before switching devices.
learningCenter_export_summary: Use PDF to apply and JSON to restore editing.
learningCenter_export_step1: Select Export Resume in the header and choose local PDF or another format.
learningCenter_export_step2: Export long images as PNG or PDF, or choose Markdown, HTML, or full JSON.
learningCenter_export_step3: Open the file and check page breaks, fonts, images, and links.
learningCenter_export_tip: Cloud export is unavailable. Use local export.
learningCenter_privacy_summary: Hide selected sensitive fields without changing the original resume.
learningCenter_privacy_step1: Select Redacted Resume in the export dialog.
learningCenter_privacy_step2: Open Edit Fields and choose a preset or select individual fields.
learningCenter_privacy_step3: Open the exported file to check sensitive information and pagination.
learningCenter_privacy_tip: Full JSON retains original data and is not a redacted sharing file.
moduleHelp_user_description: Include your name, target role, and reliable contact details so recruiters can quickly understand who you are and how to reach you. Select other details based on the role, and check your phone number, email, and links before applying.
moduleHelp_user_question1: Do I need to fill in every personal detail?
moduleHelp_user_answer1: No. Prioritize your name, target role, and contact details. Include other information only when relevant or requested. Hide fields you do not need instead of adding unrelated details to fill space.
moduleHelp_user_question2: Are a photo and school logo required?
moduleHelp_user_answer2: Neither is required. If you use a photo, choose a clear, natural professional portrait. Add a school logo if it suits your layout. You can adjust or hide both in their respective fields.
moduleHelp_slogan_description: Use a short title or sentence to express your career direction and relevant strengths. Keep it consistent with the rest of your resume and avoid vague slogans or a lengthy introduction.
moduleHelp_slogan_question1: How long should the slogan be?
moduleHelp_slogan_answer1: Keep it easy to read at a glance. Use a concise title and focus the subtitle on one point. Check the preview to make sure the text fits the header.
moduleHelp_slogan_question2: What if I do not have a suitable slogan?
moduleHelp_slogan_answer2: Use a simple career title or hide content you do not need. There is no need to fill the header with a slogan unrelated to your experience.
moduleHelp_account_description: Choose profiles that demonstrate your professional abilities. Include the platform, account name, and a working profile link. Prioritize portfolios, code, or professional content.
moduleHelp_account_question1: Should I include every social account?
moduleHelp_account_answer1: Include accounts relevant to your application and suitable for public viewing. Leave out private or unrelated profiles to keep attention on your professional work.
moduleHelp_account_question2: What should I check about profile links?
moduleHelp_account_answer2: Use a complete profile URL and check whether access requires a login or special permission. Open each link before applying and make sure it leads to your profile rather than the platform homepage.
moduleHelp_education_description: State your school, major, degree, and attendance dates. Add relevant coursework, research, practical work, or achievements when they support the target role. Avoid repeating the basic fields in the description.
moduleHelp_education_question1: Should I include coursework and grades?
moduleHelp_education_answer1: Choose based on relevance. Add courses that demonstrate useful foundations. Include grades or rankings when they are a verifiable strength, and explain the ranking scope instead of listing a full transcript.
moduleHelp_education_question2: How much detail is needed after years of work?
moduleHelp_education_answer2: Usually keep the school, major, degree, and dates, leaving more space for recent work achievements. Add research or academic details when they directly support the target role.
moduleHelp_skill_description: Choose skills you actually have that are relevant to the role. Explain proficiency, practical use, or problems you have solved. Group skills when helpful and avoid unsupported lists or exaggerated expertise.
moduleHelp_skill_question1: Is a longer skill list better?
moduleHelp_skill_answer1: Prioritize skills the role needs and that you can explain through practical experience. Omit tools you barely know so your main strengths remain clear.
moduleHelp_skill_answer2: Explain what you can do independently and where you have applied the skill. If you use the proficiency list layout, choose levels that match your actual experience.
moduleHelp_advantage_description: Choose strengths relevant to the role that your experience can support. Use a specific situation, your actions, and the result to explain each strength instead of listing personality labels alone.
moduleHelp_advantage_question1: Can I say I am a fast learner or responsible?
moduleHelp_advantage_answer1: Yes, but support the claim with facts. Explain what you learned, how you took responsibility, and what you delivered rather than relying on adjectives alone.
moduleHelp_advantage_question2: How do I avoid repeating work experience?
moduleHelp_advantage_answer2: Summarize abilities that appear across your experience and support them briefly. Keep detailed actions in the relevant experience section instead of copying the same paragraph twice.
moduleHelp_work_description: State the employer, role, and dates, then connect your responsibilities with specific actions and actual results. Use context, action, and result to organize your thoughts, prioritizing contributions relevant to the target role.
moduleHelp_work_question1: How can I show results without metrics?
moduleHelp_work_answer1: Describe real deliverables, problems solved, process changes, or quality improvements, and explain your role. Use verified numbers when available; do not invent percentages or claim the entire team's results as your own.
moduleHelp_work_question2: How should I choose among many experiences?
moduleHelp_work_answer2: Give more space to recent, relevant experience and summarize older or less relevant roles. Combine similar responsibilities and focus on actions and results that distinguish your contribution.
moduleHelp_internship_description: State the organization, role, and internship dates. Explain your tasks, the parts you handled, and what you produced. Even a limited assignment can demonstrate ability through a clear process and deliverable.
moduleHelp_internship_question1: What if most of my work was supporting others?
moduleHelp_internship_answer1: Explain whom you supported, the steps you performed, and what you delivered, such as research, analysis, or event execution. Use accurate verbs rather than presenting support work as independent leadership.
moduleHelp_internship_question2: Is a short internship worth including?
moduleHelp_internship_answer2: Yes, if it is relevant and involved real tasks or outputs. State the actual dates and contribution without extending the duration or inventing achievements.
moduleHelp_project_description: Explain the project's context, goal, your role, key contributions, and actual outcome. Highlight what you owned, the methods you used, and the challenges you solved while distinguishing personal contributions from team results.
moduleHelp_project_question1: How do I show my contribution to a team project?
moduleHelp_project_answer1: Briefly introduce the goal, then state your scope, key decisions, and completed work. Team metrics can provide context, but explain how your own work contributed to them.
moduleHelp_project_question2: Can I include coursework or personal projects?
moduleHelp_project_answer2: Yes, when they are real and relevant. Identify the project type and describe the problem, implementation, and demonstrable output. Do not present a classroom exercise as a commercially launched product.
moduleHelp_club_description: State the organization, role, and participation dates. Focus on organizing activities, collaborating, executing tasks, and producing results that demonstrate abilities relevant to the target role.
moduleHelp_club_question1: Can I include experience as a regular member?
moduleHelp_club_answer1: Yes. Focus on actual tasks such as creating promotional materials, coordinating venues, organizing registrations, or running an event. You do not need a leadership title to have useful experience.
moduleHelp_club_question2: Should I list every club activity?
moduleHelp_club_answer2: Choose activities that best demonstrate relevant abilities and explain your tasks and results. Summarize similar activities instead of listing names without context.
moduleHelp_volunteer_description: Describe the organization, service, participation dates, and your responsibilities. Use real records to explain whom you served, your effort, and your outputs, emphasizing actual actions and collaboration.
moduleHelp_volunteer_question1: Do I have to include volunteer hours?
moduleHelp_volunteer_answer1: Include hours when you have reliable records and they help explain your commitment. Otherwise, describe the dates and service itself without guessing or inflating the hours.
moduleHelp_volunteer_question2: How can volunteering relate to my target role?
moduleHelp_volunteer_answer2: Identify abilities shown by real tasks, such as communication, coordination, event execution, information management, or professional services. Demonstrate them through actions without adding responsibilities you did not hold.
moduleHelp_publication_description: Include the paper title, author order, venue, and current publication status, with an accessible link when useful. Describe the research question, methods, and your contribution, clearly distinguishing published, accepted, and submitted work.
moduleHelp_publication_question1: Can I include an unpublished paper?
moduleHelp_publication_answer1: Yes, but clearly state its actual status. A submission is not an acceptance, and an accepted paper should be distinguished from one already published.
moduleHelp_publication_question2: How should I state author order and contributions?
moduleHelp_publication_answer2: Use the actual author order and only claim co-first authorship when documented. Explain the research, experiments, analysis, or writing you handled without claiming all work on the paper.
moduleHelp_honor_description: Choose relevant or representative awards and certificates. State their names, dates, and issuing organizations accurately. Explain the award scope, level, or verification link when helpful.
moduleHelp_honor_question1: Is it better to list more certificates and awards?
moduleHelp_honor_answer1: Prioritize items relevant to the role, clearly recognized, or useful as evidence of ability. Omit repetitive or less relevant items so the strongest ones stand out.
moduleHelp_honor_question2: Can I list a certificate I am still preparing for as earned?
moduleHelp_honor_answer2: No. Describe your actual progress without presenting it as an earned qualification. Be accurate about expired certificates or those with validity limits as well.
moduleHelp_portfolio_description: Choose representative work and provide images, concise descriptions, and accessible links. Explain its purpose, your part, and the result, making sure the material is suitable for public sharing.
moduleHelp_portfolio_question1: What should I check about portfolio links?
moduleHelp_portfolio_answer1: Confirm that links work and permissions allow viewing. Link directly to the relevant work where possible. Include an access code or instructions in the description if needed.
moduleHelp_portfolio_answer2: Yes, when it is approved for public sharing and your contribution is clear. For internal or confidential material, obtain permission or use appropriately redacted public material.
moduleHelp_custom_description: Give the section a clear title and organize facts relevant to the target role. For experience, explain the context, your actions, and results. For other content, stay concise and include supporting evidence where needed.
moduleHelp_custom_question1: What belongs in a custom section?
moduleHelp_custom_answer1: You can include training, language abilities, relevant interests, or other content not covered by the preset sections. Keep each section focused on one topic and avoid duplicating existing content.
moduleHelp_custom_question2: How much detail should I include?
moduleHelp_custom_answer2: Include enough for readers to understand what you have done and what you can do. Prioritize specific, verifiable information and expand when you have meaningful experience rather than adding unrelated filler.
resumeExampleGuide_work: Set the role context and goal, then describe your responsibilities and key actions, followed by verifiable business, efficiency, or quality results. If metrics are unavailable, state the actual deliverable without estimating.
resumeExampleGuide_project: Describe the project context, goal, or challenge, then clarify your ownership, key actions, and actual results. Separate your contribution from the team's; mark missing outcomes for follow-up.
resumeExampleGuide_education: List your school, degree, major, and attendance dates. Add coursework, research, practice, or achievements that support the target role, and clarify your contribution; omit unrelated details.
resumeExampleGuide_skill: Choose skills relevant to the target role and group them by your actual proficiency. Use a task or project to show how you applied each skill and what problem it solved; avoid listing tools alone.
resumeExampleGuide_advantage: Choose strengths that your resume can verify, then use a specific situation, your actions, and the result to show them. Avoid unsupported claims such as “fast learner” or “detail-oriented.”
resumeExampleGuide_publication: State the paper title, author order, publication venue, and status. In the body, describe the research question, the methods used, and your own contribution, and include indexing or quartile labels when available.

moduleHelp_jobIntent_description: Group your target role, job search status, availability, preferred city, and expected salary. Drag the handle beside a field to reorder it in the preview and exports. Adding this module moves completed fields from Personal Information. Your work start date stays there. Use the display settings beside the title to choose text labels, icons, or values only independently.
moduleHelp_jobIntent_question1: Why are these fields no longer in Personal Information?
moduleHelp_jobIntent_answer1: While Job Preferences exists, these five fields are edited and displayed there. Your name, contact details, and work start date remain in Personal Information.
moduleHelp_jobIntent_question2: Will deleting or hiding this module lose my information?
moduleHelp_jobIntent_answer2: Deleting moves the latest nonempty fields to the end of Personal Information without restoring their original order or pinned positions. Cleared fields do not recover old values. Hiding only affects preview and exports; it does not move or delete data.

resumePhotoQuestion: Should you include a photo on your resume?
photoUsageTip: Photo guidance: generally recommended for private and state-owned companies and Chinese resumes; often optional for foreign companies and English resumes.
photoUsageAdvice: If you include a photo, use a professional headshot and avoid casual or AI-generated images.
photoPrintQuestion: Should the photo be printed in color or black and white?
photoPrintColorAdvice: Color printing: recommended; it keeps the skin tones and background colors of a formal photo.
photoPrintGrayAdvice: Black-and-white printing: not recommended; grayscale makes the portrait look dull and washed out.
photoCropAdvice: Crop: leave a little space above the head and show the shoulders; avoid a tight head-only crop.
photoBackgroundAdvice: Background: white, blue, or gray is recommended; red is generally not advised.
photoAppearanceAdvice: Appearance: smile naturally, keep your hair neat, and avoid covering your face.
photoClothingAdvice: Clothing: formal industries may call for a suit; darker shirts or T-shirts work well for tech roles.
photoProcessingTip: The image is cropped and compressed to the avatar ratio and used only for your resume photo.
